source_evidence: Some financial experts advise rebalancing at regular intervals, such as every six or 12 months. Others recommend rebalancing when your holdings of an asset class increase or decrease more than a pre-set percentage. In either case, rebalancing tends to work best when done relatively infrequently.
question: Misconception: To keep my portfolio on target, I should rebalance very frequently whenever its asset mix changes by even a small amount.
answer: The source does not recommend constant rebalancing. It describes two approaches: rebalancing at regular intervals, such as every six or 12 months, or when an asset class moves beyond a preset percentage. It also says rebalancing tends to work best when done relatively infrequently.
